- Policy stance: The statement is still moderately hawkish (25 bp hike to 4.50–4.75%, “ongoing increases,” and continued QT; IORB 4.65% and ON RRP 4.55% maintain firm control of short rates).
- SLOOS overlay: The latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows broad-based tightening in credit and weaker loan demand:
  - Banks tightened standards for C&I and CRE loans; foreign banks also report weaker C&I demand.
  - Weaker demand across nonfarm nonresidential, construction/land development, and multifamily CRE.
  - Firms cite decreased financing needs for plant/equipment, M&A, inventories, and accounts receivable.
- Implications: Tighter bank lending standards plus softer demand point to a meaningful endogenous tightening of financial conditions that should weigh on capex and activity, reinforcing the Committee’s emphasis on cumulative tightening and policy lags and reducing the need for an aggressively hawkish path.
- Net: Still a hawkish bias, but SLOOS-driven credit tightening tempers that stance further toward neutral.
